text:
Hey, listen! You know how my grandma keeps that big jar of peppermint candies on the counter? Well, she never eats them herself. She just waits for someone to come by. One day, a tiny mouse with a torn ear scurried in, shivering and looking super sad. He didn’t have any food, but he had this shiny blue marble he found in the garden.

The mouse tried to trade the marble for one candy, but Grandma smiled and gave him three instead. "Keep your treasure," she said. "I already have plenty." The mouse was so happy he danced on his hind legs. Years later, when Grandma’s eyes got blurry and she forgot where her glasses were, who do you think found them? The mouse! He remembered every single time she was kind to him.

See, it’s like this: when you give something away, it doesn’t disappear. It stays in people’s hearts like a secret note. Generosity is basically making sure someone remembers you fondly, even if they forget everything else. So, sharing isn’t just nice; it’s like planting seeds that turn into memories. Cool, right?
